13.0.s.en: 1. The sanctification of the land and its inhabitants:

13.0.0.en: 1 "In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness. 2 And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered: and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land. 3 And it shall come to pass, that when any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of the LORD: and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth. 4 And it shall come to pass in that day, that the prophets shall be ashamed every one of his vision, when he hath prophesied; neither shall they wear a rough garment to deceive: 5 But he shall say, I am no prophet, I am an husbandman; for a man hath possessed me from my youth. 6 And one shall say unto him, What are these wounds in thine hands? Then he shall answer, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends."

13.0.1.en: He speaks of the mystery of the sanctification of the land (the body) and its inhabitants (the soul) through the fountain of the divine Blood, which cleanses from every sin and uncleanness, removes from us every unclean spirit, and destroys in us everything that is not of God, saying: "In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness. And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered: and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land" [1-2].

13.0.2.en: What is this fountain opened for us, the house of David, since we have become kings in it, and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that is, those who enjoy the vision of peace, which takes away sin and uncleanness, if not the wounds of the Lord Jesus?! It is the fountain of cleansing for us and at the same time the cause of judgment for the wicked. This is the fountain that never runs dry, so the Church continues to drink from it all the days of her life and is sanctified in it continually.

13.0.3.en: St. Didymus the Blind comments on this fountain, saying: [This sprinkling or pouring out is accomplished by the divine Blood of the Savior, of which St. Peter speaks... "Unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace unto you, and peace, be multiplied"... as he says: "Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver or gold... But with the precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot" (1 Pet 1:18-19). Those who thus submit to the shed Blood receive a clean heart, saying, as though they were one person, in their repeated prayers without ceasing: "Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow," that they may obtain the purity of which it was said: "Pure religion and undefiled"].

13.0.4.en: This is our living fountain in which we are washed and cleansed from every uncleanness, and through it the names of the idols are cut off from the land, that everything belonging to the devil may be removed from the land of our body, so that it is no longer the land of his kingdom. If the Law forbade pronouncing the names of the pagan gods, it was so that no stranger should be remembered in our body, but God alone should reign over it. Sanctification does not stop at removing the names of the idols but extends to removing the false prophets who work on their behalf, and also removing the unclean spirit, which is the spirit of error and falsehood.

13.1.0.en: The power of the holy life appears in his saying that when the godly parents mourn for their sins they do not leave their son to play the part of a false prophet, preferring to pierce their son with a spear so that he dies rather than allow him the false prophecy [3]. Thus through the holy life evil is removed completely and the false prophets are exposed and put to shame, and they do not wear a rough garment to deceive [4], so they do not wear the austere garb of the prophets, but deny that they are prophets. Thus God pours out upon His people the spirit of grace and sanctification, so that they are not deceived by false appearances and do not tolerate error.

13.2.0.en: If anyone asks them about their wounds, since the prophets of the idols, especially of Baal, were known to cut themselves when they inquired of the gods (1 Kgs 18:28), each one of them answers out of fear and shame that he is not a prophet but merely a farmer who was wounded in the house of his friends and not in worship [5-6].

13.2.1.en: It is wonderful that while the false prophet in his deceit hides the real cause of his wounds, hiding that he wounded himself in misleading worship, the Lord Christ, the true Word of God, was truly wounded in the house of His friends, for His disciple betrayed Him and His own delivered Him to death... as though God brings forth, even from the words of the wicked, a true prophecy concerning what was to be accomplished in the person of the Messiah.

13.3.0.en: 7 "Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the LORD of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones. 8 And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the LORD, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein. 9 And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The LORD is my God."

13.3.1.en: While the false prophet equivocates about his wounds, the Lord Christ announces His wounds beforehand in the spirit of prophecy, for it was said: "Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the LORD of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones" [7].

13.3.2.en: St. John Chrysostom says: [Satan rages with great violence against the teachers, because by their destruction the flock is scattered. By slaughtering the sheep the flock is diminished, but by striking the shepherd the whole flock perishes... by one soul all perish]. This is what Satan thought he could do by striking the Messiah the Savior; he thought that by striking the Shepherd the sheep would be scattered, so that he might turn his hand and rule over the little ones]. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Matthew the Evangelist wrote concerning this prophecy when Jesus was arrested and His disciples fled: "That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets" (Mt 2:23), "I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad" (Mt 26:31). It is understood from the word "smite" and other words concerning death that the Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep (Jn 10:15), gives His life a ransom for many (Mt 20:28)].

13.4.0.en: Through these wounds the Lord says that two parts of the inhabitants of the earth "shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein. And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The LORD is my God" [8-9].

13.4.1.en: If, because of the rejection of the wounds of the Lord, or the rejection of the wounded Lord on behalf of mankind, two parts of the earth are cut off from the land of the living and die eternally, then the third part enters under the fire of affliction, to share with their wounded Savior in His wounds; or, in other words, they bear their wounds in them as a sign of their union with Him.

13.4.2.en: Through affliction the Church enters the furnace of the Cross, that the word of God may be proclaimed in her as silver purified seven times (Ps 12:6), and her life may be proclaimed as refined gold, that is, a heavenly, spiritual life full of true riches and eternal glory. If silver signifies the word of God, so every soul that desires to bear true silver, that is, a witness to the word of God, and to become of a heavenly nature (not earthly) and spiritual (not fleshly), possessing true riches and authority, is fitting to be tried by the fire of the Cross. Such a soul hears the divine voice saying: "It is my people," that is, He joins her to the true membership of His heavenly Church, while she sings joyfully to Him, saying: "The LORD is my God"!

14.0.0.en: "1 Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, and thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee. 2 For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city shall be taken, and the houses rifled, and the women ravished; and half of the city shall go forth into captivity, and the residue of the people shall not be cut off from the city." [1-2].

14.0.1.en: At the end of the previous chapter we saw that two parts of the earth are cut off and die, while the third remains in it, refined by fire like silver and tried like gold. As St. Didymus the Blind sees it, the two parts are the pagans and the Jews who reject salvation, while the third is the company of believers who were set free from the satanic captivity by the Cross and received the divine fire that gives sanctification, of which St. John the Baptist said: "He shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire" (Mt 3:11), as the Lord Himself said: "I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?!" (Lk 12:49). St. Didymus the Blind sees that it is also the fire of trials that refines the soul, for he says: [Those who passed through the fire, that is, the last third of the captives who were purified and whose prayer the Lord answered, say to God who gave them peace: "For thou, O God, hast proved us: thou hast tried us, as silver is tried. Thou broughtest us into the net; thou laidst affliction upon our loins. Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place" (Ps 66:10-12). And in Isaiah also God the Savior of man says: "Fear not: for I am with thee. When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be scorched; neither shall the flame burn thee..." (Isa 43:3-4). How can there be walking in the fire and coming out of it without loss, unless we have the voice of the Lord, of whom it was said that He quenches the flame of the fire? For as the Red Sea was divided by the stroke of the holy rod and the people passed through without loss, so the flame of the fire is divided and opens for passage through it without burning].

14.0.2.en: The divine fire, whether the fire of the Holy Spirit who gives sanctification or the fire of the refining trials, increases the believer in radiance and glory, but the stubborn are shattered by it. Therefore he says: "Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, and thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee" [1]. The day of the Lord is a day of salvation for the submissive souls and their liberation from their captivity, but it is a harsh and bitter day for the arrogant souls that cling to their evil. As was said by the prophet Isaiah: "Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it" (Isa 13:9).

14.0.3.en: The spoils are usually divided outside the captured city, lest the captors be occupied with the booty and the captives recover their strength and fight them. But here he says: "Thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee," a sign of the enemies' contempt for the city and their realization that it is utterly shattered, with no possibility of her rising again. The hideousness of this contempt appears in their dividing the women among themselves as booty, to commit evil with them before their husbands, as was said by Isaiah: "Their children also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be spoiled, and their wives ravished" (Isa 13:16).

14.0.4.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that the divine wrath came upon Jerusalem to the uttermost (1 Thess 2:16) because of her killing of the Lord and His disciples, so she fell under the might of Justus the Roman commander, who destroyed her completely in a hideous manner recorded by Josephus the Jewish historian.

14.0.5.en: It is a painful picture of the soul that falls into the captivity of the devil through unbelief, so the enemy storms its depths and humiliates it within, and stirs up all the sins (the nations) against it, so he plunders every good thing in it and defiles the body (the women) with all its faculties, and every fruit (the children) is shattered.

14.1.0.en: It is wonderful that half of the city is carried into captivity outside, while the residue is not cut off from the city [2]. The first half signifies the old Jerusalem, or the Jews who reject the Savior, while the residue signifies those who accepted faith in Him, upon whom the Church, the new Jerusalem, was established. At the same time the first half signifies the old outer man who must be driven out, while the residue signifies the inner man who is renewed. May the old die and the new live in us!

14.2.s.en: 2. On the Mount of Olives (the Lord bears our sufferings in us):

14.2.0.en: 3 Then shall the LORD go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle. 4 And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west, and there shall be a very great valley; and half of the mountain shall remove toward the north, and half of it toward the south. 5 And ye shall flee to the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach unto Azal: yea, ye shall flee, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: and the LORD my God shall come, and all the saints with thee.

14.2.1.en: As the old, literal, legal Jerusalem is shattered so that the new, spiritual Jerusalem may arise in us, that the Lord may dwell in her and fight for her and support her, revealing His Cross in her, he says: "Then shall the LORD go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle. And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west, and there shall be a very great valley; and half of the mountain shall remove toward the north, and half of it toward the south. And ye shall flee to the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach unto Azal: yea, ye shall flee, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: and the LORD my God shall come, and all the saints with thee" [3-5].

14.2.2.en: Since man fell under the captivity of the devil and collapsed before the sins (the nations), his Creator came forward to set him free, for it was said: "Then shall the LORD go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle" [3]. The Lord Himself came forward to fight the devil with all his evils, to free man from his power. St. Didymus the Blind comments on the word "go forth," saying: [Yes, our Lord and Savior says of Himself in the Gospel: "For I proceeded forth and came from God (the Father); neither came I of myself, but he sent me" (Jn 8:42). In the same sense Habakkuk says to God: "Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, for the salvation of thine anointed; thou crushedst the head of the house of the wicked, laying bare the foundation unto the neck" (Hab 3:13). And as He goes forth and comes to those whom He saves, so He goes forth more clearly when He makes war (against the devil). It is written in the book of Micah: "For, behold, the LORD cometh forth out of his place, and will come down, and tread upon the high places of the earth" (Mic 1:13), and in Isaiah: The LORD shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war: he shall cry, yea, roar; he shall prevail against his enemies" (Isa 42:13)].

14.2.3.en: The Lord goes forth to fight for us, and stands in that day, the day of redemption, upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mountain cleaves in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west to make a very great valley, and half of the mountain removes toward the north and half of it toward the south... What does this mean?

14.2.4.en: First: The Savior stood upon the mount of Olives east of Jerusalem as the Sower who planted the holy olive trees of which it was said: "But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God" (Ps 52:9), "thy children like olive plants round about thy table" (Ps 128:3). These trees, as St. Didymus says: [are not planted in the valley on the west, but on the mountain on high toward the east, and the Sun of Righteousness shines upon them with His divine light, as though they were the trees that the Lord planted in Paradise, in the garden of Eden eastward (Gen 2:8). Each of them hears the voice of the Crucified: "To day shalt thou be with me in paradise" (Lk 23:43), so the holy trees say with the Apostle: "But our conversation is in heaven" (Phil 3:20)].

14.2.5.en: Second: If we have been planted by Christ Jesus the Crucified as olive trees in the house of God east of Jerusalem, then we stand there with the disciples, contemplating the ascension of the Lord at the mount of Olives, awaiting His coming as the angel said (Acts 1:12).

14.3.0.en: Third: By faith we were planted east of Jerusalem on the holy mountain, but the Jews, by their denial of the Messiah the Savior, descended into the very great valley toward the west [4], and with them all who deny the divine grace, and the valley is like the chasm that separates those planted in the east from those in the west.

14.3.1.en: Fourth: Half of the mountain removes toward the north, where the cold north wind is, and the other half toward the south, where the warm, hot wind is. The first half signifies the coldness of the spirit, or evil, and the other signifies the heat of the Spirit (the spiritual noonday). St. Didymus sees, in the words of the bride: "Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits" (Song 4:16), that the north wind signifies the devil, where the bitter cold destroys the crop and hinders the breezes of the divine fragrance, while the south wind, by its heat and its fragrance, inflames the soul, representing the Lord the Savior, who said: "I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?!" (Lk 12:49).

14.3.2.en: Let us say to the north wind, not with the tongue but with deeds, that it turn away far from us by fulfilling the words of the Apostle: "Abstain from all appearance of evil" (1 Thess 5:22), and let us call the south wind by receiving the Lord Christ in our life in practice!

14.4.0.en: Fifth: St. Didymus sees, in the saying: "the valley of the mountains shall reach unto Azal" [5], that the ravine between the mountains reaches to Asahel, of whom it was said: "light of foot as a wild roe" (2 Sam 2:18). The believer in Christ Jesus runs among the holy mountains with light, swift feet toward his Bridegroom, with piercing spiritual glances toward Him.

14.4.1.en: Sixth: He says: "Yea, ye shall flee, like as ye fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah: and the LORD my God shall come, and all the saints with thee" [5]. This famous earthquake is the one that happened in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, and Amos mentioned it (Amos 1:1). And when Uzziah knew his sin toward the holy things by burning incense on the altar of incense (2 Chr 26:16), he was struck with leprosy in his forehead before the priests in the house of the LORD and was driven out from there, and his son was set up in his place. So fleeing from the earthquake means our fleeing from what befell Uzziah, from the leprosy of his sin, that we may enjoy the indwelling of the Lord our God in us, that He may reign within us.

14.4.2.en: Let us flee from the earthquake of Uzziah to receive the earthquake of the Cross, through which many of the dead went into Jerusalem and appeared to many (Mt 27:51-52), that it may shake our earthly, dusty mind and raise up in us the living, spiritual mind.

14.5.s.en: 3. The Cross as a known day:

14.5.0.en: 6 And it shall come to pass in that day, that there shall be no light. The luminaries shall be drawn in. 7 But it shall be one day which shall be known to the LORD, not day, nor night: but it shall come to pass, that at evening time it shall be light. [6-7].

14.5.1.en: For as he speaks of the Cross in our life, he separates the trees planted in the east from those in the west, and those that receive the south wind from those that receive the north wind, and those that carry the Cross, hastening to Asahel with light feet and piercing sight toward their crucified Bridegroom, from the denying soul, and those that reject the earthquake of Uzziah from those that bow down to it... All this is fulfilled in the day of the Cross, which he described thus:

14.5.2.en: First: "There shall be no light," for darkness fell at the time of the Cross, revealing the authority that was given to darkness, but only for a time.

14.5.3.en: Second: "One day which shall be known to the LORD," and as St. Didymus says: [The day of the Lord is continuous, no night cuts it off]; it is the day of eternal light (Isa 60:9).

14.6.0.en: Third: "Not day, nor night: but it shall come to pass, that at evening time it shall be light" [7]. It is not day because darkness covered the earth, nor is it night because it was the time of day; it is neither day nor night, but at evening time there is light, for the outer darkness was dispelled after the ninth hour, as the inner darkness was dispelled through the work of the Cross in the life of mankind.

14.7.s.en: 4. The outpouring of the Holy Spirit and the Church:

14.7.0.en: 8 And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea: in summer and in autumn shall it be. 9 And the LORD shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall the LORD be alone, and his name alone. 10 All the land shall be turned as a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem: and it shall be lifted up, and inhabited in her place, from Benjamin's gate unto the place of the first gate, unto the corner gate, and from the tower of Hananeel unto the king's winepresses. 11 And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more curse; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.

14.7.1.en: "And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea: in summer and in autumn shall it be" [8]. What are these waters but the waters of the Holy Spirit, which are bound to the Cross?! In our study of the Book of Ezekiel (Ezek 47) the waters were bound to the altar, that is, to the sacrifice of the Cross. And now, as he speaks of the Cross as a known day that occupies the mind of God, the springs of the Holy Spirit burst forth, going out from Jerusalem, where the Apostles were, to the eastern sea and the western sea, that is, to the Gentiles in the east and the west. In the Septuagint it came: "the former sea and the latter sea," that is, to work in the life of the Jews who came first and enjoyed the Law and then in the life of the Gentiles. Thus the door was opened by the outpouring upon all mankind, as the Lord said: "And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh" (Joel 2:28), and by this the name of God is glorified in all.

14.7.2.en: St. Didymus sees that these living waters that go out from Jerusalem to pour into the eastern and western seas are the spiritual Law, or divine knowledge, or divine love, things that overflow in the Church, the Jerusalem above, to work in the world for its sanctification, for he says: [This idea has crystallized from our interpretation: "They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea" (Isa 11:9); it is filled with the divine love that is from God, which overflows upon the chosen and covers a multitude of sins (Jas 5:20), covering the evil deeds so that nothing of them remains; so the knowledge of the Lord is water that covers the sea and turns it into sweet and pure waters].

14.7.3.en: We may say that our souls have become an eastern sea struck by self-righteousness (the blow from the right), or a western sea struck by the blows from the left; so we are in need of the work of the Holy Spirit in us to remove from us the salinity of our own waters and the salinity of the waters of evil, into the sweetness of the holy river that makes glad the city of God.

14.8.0.en: Through these new, sweet waters, that is, the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, God reigns over the Church spread throughout the world, for he says: "And the LORD shall be king over the earth: in that day shall the LORD be alone, and his name alone" [9]... He reigns not over the Jews alone but also over the Gentiles who come to the Lord. And as St. Didymus says: [Formerly there was a difference between the eastern and western seas, that is, between the Jews and the Greeks. Not all acknowledge the oneness of God, for the pagans believe in many gods, while the Jews have one God; but when the Gospel came, the knowledge of the one and only Creator spread among all. Paul writes: "Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also: seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision by faith" (Rom 3:29)... The Lord shall be alone in that day which the LORD hath made (Ps 118:24), when the Sun of Righteousness arises (Mal 4:2), and His name alone also, for when all mankind are united in thought and blameless godliness they will have one name that points to God. By this the saying of the Psalm is fulfilled: "How wonderful is thy holy name in all the earth!" (Ps 8:1), and also: "Thou hast magnified thy holy name upon the earth" (Ps 137:2)... and by this the petition offered to God is fulfilled: "Hallowed be thy name"]...

14.9.0.en: The prophet continues his speech, saying: "All the land shall be turned as a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem: and it shall be lifted up, and inhabited in her place, from Benjamin's gate unto the place of the first gate, unto the corner gate, and from the tower of Hananeel unto the king's winepresses. And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more curse; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited" [10-11].

14.9.1.en: By these phrases he reveals the dimensions of the Church in which the Holy Spirit works as living waters flowing through the Cross, that the name of God alone may be glorified on the earth, and they can be summarized as follows:

14.9.2.en: First: He says: "All the land shall be turned as a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem." Since "Geba" in St. Didymus' view means "testimony," and "Rimmon" means "a high or lofty place," in his opinion the dimensions of the knowledge of the Lord with which the Church overflows are the testimony to the Lord by the high (heavenly) Spirit. We may say that the Church in which the waters of the Holy Spirit overflow extends in the life of mankind from Geba, that is, from testimony to God in Christ Jesus, as the righteousness of God working in us, to bring us to Rimmon, that is, to lead us into the exalted, lofty life. As for Rimmon being south of Jerusalem, as we saw before, the south wind is hot and inflames our Jerusalem with the Spirit who neither cools nor grows lukewarm.

14.9.3.en: Second: "It shall be lifted up, and inhabited in her place" [10]. Since the soul is lifted up to Rimmon, it is fitting that we should not cease to be lifted up, and as St. Didymus says: [It carries a power from on high to be lifted up and not to descend, for it is fitting for those who have reached the goal and arrived at perfection itself through striving to stand firm in holiness].

14.9.4.en: Third: "From Benjamin's gate unto the place of the first gate, unto the corner gate" [10]. The living Church sets out from Benjamin's gate, that is, the gate of the son of the right hand, so she is like her Bridegroom who sits at the right hand of the Majesty; she has no members on the left, but all are sons of the right hand, that is, heirs of glory. The Church goes forth to the corner gate, so she is like the Lord, the cornerstone which the builders rejected (Ps 118:22; Isa 28:16; Eph 2:20; 1 Pet 2:6), and He joined the Jews with the Gentiles in one integrated building. So the Church, like her Bridegroom, binds all together by the Holy Spirit to be one holy sanctuary to the Lord.

14.9.5.en: Therefore, let us enter by Benjamin's gate, which is called "the first gate," which none enters but he who is hidden in the Lord Christ, who says with boldness and power: "Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and I will praise the LORD" (Ps 118:19), "This gate of the LORD, into which the righteous shall enter" (Ps 118:20). Let us enter this gate and be joined to the cornerstone, rejected by men and glorified by God, and let us not be like the hypocrites, who do not enter the heavenly gate but stand in the corners making long prayers to seek the praise of men.

14.9.6.en: Fourth: "From the tower of Hananeel unto the king's winepresses" [10]. The word "Hananeel" in Hebrew means "God has been gracious" or "has shown favor"; it is a tower near the Sheep Gate and the tower of Meah as renewed by Nehemiah (Neh 3:1; 12:39). And the king's winepresses signify the spiritual house of wine (Song 2:4), which symbolizes inward joy. So the Church of the New Testament is characterized by the tower of "the free grace of God," of which the Lord spoke to His disciples, saying: "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him" (Lk 14:28-29). Thus a man begins his life in the Church by counting the cost: Does he have faith in the free grace of God? Can he enjoy the surpassing divine tower so that he may be fortified in it, saying: "For thou hast been a refuge for me, and a strong tower from the enemy. I will abide in thy tabernacle for ever: I will trust in the covert of thy wings" (Ps 61:3-4). Through this tower the believer goes forth to the king's winepresses, that is, to the house of wine, to be pressed with the Lord who passed through the winepress, to enjoy the joy of the Holy Spirit!

14.10.0.en: Fifth: "And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more curse; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited" [11]. In place of the desolation that befell the soul because of sin, she is filled with glory and life, so she is inhabited not only by people but by God Himself, who sanctifies her, so she is enlarged with love for all mankind, and thus she comes out of the state of gloomy desolation to the state of fullness with the grace of God and love of neighbor and the sense of surpassing peace and inner security.

14.11.s.en: 5. The pulling down of the old man and the rising of the new:

14.11.0.en: 12 And this shall be the plague wherewith the LORD will smite all the people that have fought against Jerusalem; Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth. 13 And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great tumult from the LORD shall be among them; and they shall lay hold every one on the hand of his neighbour, and his hand shall rise up against the hand of his neighbour. 14 And Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the nations round about shall be gathered together, gold, and silver, and apparel, in great abundance. 15 And so shall be the plague of the horse, of the mule, of the camel, and of the ass, and of all the beasts that shall be in these tents, as this plague. 16 And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles. 17 And it shall be, that whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain. 18 And if the family of Egypt go not up, and come not, that have no rain; there shall be the plague, wherewith the LORD will smite the nations that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles. 19 This shall be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all nations that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles. 20 In that day shall there be upon the bells of the horses, "HOLINESS UNTO THE LORD"; and the pots in the LORD'S house shall be like the bowls before the altar. 21 Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness unto the LORD of hosts: and all they that sacrifice shall come and take of them, and seethe therein: and in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the LORD of hosts.

14.11.1.en: The prophet concludes his speech about the saving work of God in His holy Church, whose dimensions we have seen, by revealing the necessity of pulling down the old man with all his evil works and the rising of the new man, holy in the Lord, declaring the following:

14.11.2.en: First: He declares the plague that strikes the pagan nations that surrounded Jerusalem to fight her, as a symbol of the works of the old man or the warfare of the sins, and he says: "Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth" [12]. If the body, before its sanctification, with its evil lusts represents the old man, then this body that carries enmity against God (Rom 8:7) melts away. And lest anyone think that the body in itself is evil, he said: "Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet," for what befalls the body is not the dissolution of its material being but of its old lusts, that it may bear sanctification in it; and so also their eyes consume away in their holes, that is, they are loosed from their old glances to receive a new inner spiritual insight that befits the new man, and their tongue consumes away in their mouth, so the tongue is not destroyed in itself but dies to its evil to offer a holy voice befitting the new life. So the destruction does not touch the body and its members in themselves but strikes the evil hidden in them, that blessing and righteousness may take its place.

14.12.0.en: Second: "And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great tumult from the LORD shall be among them; and they shall lay hold every one on the hand of his neighbour, and his hand shall rise up against the hand of his neighbour" [13]. St. Didymus explains the tumult here not as the loss of peace but as the sense of great wonder before the work of God, which bewilders the soul and makes it unable to comprehend His mysteries, as in the saying: "shall fear the LORD and his goodness in the latter days" (Hos 3:5), or "I have heard thy speech, and was afraid" (Hab 3:2). So every soul marvels before the work of God, and the man takes hold of the hand of his neighbor, so all walk together in one spirit in their spiritual striving.

14.13.0.en: Third: "And Judah also shall fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the nations round about shall be gathered together, gold, and silver, and apparel, in great abundance" [14]. Who is this Judah who fights at Jerusalem and not against Jerusalem, to gather on her behalf the wealth of the nations, gold and silver and abundant apparel, but the person of the Lord Christ, who came forth from the tribe of Judah, that is, the true Judah, dwelling in our inner Jerusalem, who fights the spiritual war for us as long as He dwells in us, to seize as booty for Himself the abilities and energies that were formerly used for evil, and to use them for our spiritual edification?! He is the true King who fights in the soul to give her victory and riches, so that she is adorned for Him as a heavenly queen?

14.13.1.en: If gold signifies the spirit or heaven, and silver speech or the divine word, and apparel the gifts, then our Bridegroom who dwells in us fights against the devil for the sanctification of our spirit and our mind and all our gifts.

14.14.0.en: Fourth: "And so shall be the plague of the horse, of the mule, of the camel, and of the ass, and of all the beasts that shall be in these tents, as this plague" [15].

14.14.1.en: St. Didymus sees that these animals signify the sins that the Spirit strikes, that is, the sins of the old man that must be abandoned. In his opinion the horse signifies a man's desire for his brother's wife, as the Scripture says: "They were as fed horses roaming at large; every one neighed after his neighbour's wife" (Jer 5:8). The mules signify the barrenness of the spirit, especially of those who practice virginity of the body without enjoying the virginity and purity of the spirit, so a man is like a eunuch not for the sake of the Kingdom but for the sake of people's admiration of them (Mt 19:12). The camels signify those who care for God's law but without discernment, for they do not have the cloven hoof, so they are unclean (Lev 11:14). The asses signify lack of understanding; they are weighed down with burdens, their heads bowed toward the earth, unable to look toward the Jerusalem above.

14.14.2.en: Thus by the Holy Spirit the plague strikes these evil works under whose yoke man fell, until he is freed from them.

14.15.0.en: Fifth: He tells us of the Gentiles' enjoyment of the feast of tabernacles, for they go up to Jerusalem from year to year to worship the great King [16-19]. Not the Jews alone keep the feast, but the Gentiles enjoy this feast, where the Church of the New Testament sets out toward the heavenly Jerusalem without ceasing to sanctify the world, so men keep the feast of tabernacles, realizing that their bodies, the "tabernacles," have been sanctified to the Lord, and through them they worship the King, the LORD of hosts, until they put them off (2 Pet 1:14) to put them on again as spiritual bodies on the great day. They are the very same bodies but bear a nature befitting eternity. In this the Apostle Paul speaks to us, declaring how the believer longs not to put off the body but to bear it anew, so that death can no longer prevail over it, for he says: "For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life" (2 Cor 4:5).

14.16.0.en: Sixth: He returns to affirm the sanctification of the body by saying that upon the bells of the horses is written "Holiness unto the LORD" [20]. If the horses signify the body, then even its bells become holiness unto the Lord, meaning that there is not in the body an unclean member or an impure sense, but everything in it, within and without, is holiness unto the Lord.

14.17.0.en: Once again he affirms the holiness of everything on behalf of the Lord, saying that the pots that are in the Lord's house and every pot in Jerusalem and Judah shall be "holiness unto the LORD of hosts" [21], as though there is nothing defiled or unclean in the holy Church, but everything is like a pot or vessel that holds within it the heavenly treasure.

14.17.1.en: For the last time he affirms the same meaning by saying: "There shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the LORD of hosts" [21], that is, there is no opponent of God and no idol worshiper within the true Church, and nothing strange within the true believer.
